newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Wing Lee ends debut sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: HK's Wing Lee ends debut sharply higher.

text.p: Shares of electronic components manufacturer Wing Lee Holdings Ltd defied a weak market on Thursday to end their first trading day at HK$1.53, up HK$0.53 or 53 percent from their HK$1.00 a share issue price.
"They performed well. Investors who subscribed to the shares could make more than 50 percent profit," said Ben Kwong, research director at Dharmala Securities.

"The rally was expected in view of the strong subscription response and its small issue size, but the shares were a bit overvalued in view of the fundamentals," said Kinson Au, senior analyst at PW Asia Brokerage.
The Hang Seng Index on Thursday fell 67.98 points or 0.55 percent to close at 12,358.7.
Wing Lee shares moved in a HK$1.52 to HK$2.10 range on volume of 103.51 million shares, worth a total of HK$182.82 million.
Wing Lee manufactures DC switches, jacks, AC sockets and speaker terminals.
It issued 70 million new shares at HK$1.00 each in its initial public offer in Hong Kong, including seven million reserved for Wing Lee staff.
The offering of 63 million shares made available to the public was 312.9 times subscribed.
Brokers said they expected the shares to consolidate in the short term.
Wing Lee said the about HK$59.5 million net proceeds of the IPO would be used for working capital, to expand production facilities in Hong Kong and China and to repay bank loans.
